crux: focal length from the person's pixel height (standing frame-0 53 px vs walking 48 px vs halo-inclusive 58 px) and the aft-centreline offset from the stern silhouette extreme in the bow-to-stern back-projection along the depth-derived track heading
fault_found: both blend legs mis-scaled f: C2 used walking-frame height 48 px (f=3150, gives a 1.91 m standing person), C3 used 57-58 px including the 3-px halo/shadow below the feet plus a ~30 px square-transom offset that the rudder position (17 px inside the extreme) rules out
lesson: When a rigid object's heading comes from back-projecting its track through given depths, re-evaluate the length at several frames along the extrapolated track: a length that stays constant across the clip confirms both the heading and the along-axis motion, whereas a drifting length signals crabbing or a wrong focal length.
